svg.title: How a release reaches the Chrome Web Store
svg.desc: After every release, every day at 00:17 UTC and when started by hand with a tag, the workflow signs in to the Chrome Web Store and asks for the state of the item. A sign-in that Google turns away, a rejected release, a warning, a takedown or a review of more than 7 days fail the run, with the reason and the fix in its summary, and the bot-health sweep of the night keeps an issue open. While a review is pending, the run ends with a note, and a later day delivers the release. When the store has the release already, nothing happens. Otherwise a job without any secret takes the zip of the release, checks its signed provenance and its version and keeps it as an artifact, and a job that reaches only Google uploads it and submits it for review. A release without the zip, or a zip that fails the check, stays off the store and fails the run. When the store refuses the submission because the Developer Dashboard lacks something that the version needs, the run fails as well, and names what the release asks for beyond the version of the store. When a review began in the meantime, the run ends with the same note as for a pending review.
